title: The revision is ordered, starting with Bihar
what_changed: The Election Commission ordered a Special Intensive Revision "in the entire country", beginning with Bihar, with the schedule for the rest of the country to follow. Only electors whose enumeration forms came back would be on the draft roll. The 2003 Bihar roll was treated as evidence of eligibility, including a presumption of citizenship, and anyone not on it had to give documents from an indicative list of 11, and the younger the elector, the more they needed. Those born before 1 July 1987 gave their own, those born up to 2 December 2004 gave their own and one parent's, and those born later gave their own and both parents'. A new declaration had to go with every Form 6 for a new voter, and with Form 8 for anyone moving into Bihar. No name could be deleted from the draft without an inquiry, with appeals to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala | CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

title: Bihar's schedule
what_changed: Enumeration from 25 June to 26 July 2025, the draft roll on 1 August, claims and objections from 1 August to 1 September, and the final roll on 30 September 2025, with forms received before 25 July going into the draft.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: The 2003 roll goes online
what_changed: The 2003 Bihar roll, 4.96 crore electors, was put online. Anyone on it needed no documents, and anyone not on it could use a parent's entry in it in place of documents for that parent.
documents: CEO Bihar, press notes on the SIR, 2025

title: The Supreme Court hears the challenge
what_changed: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the 24 June order and observed that the Commission should also consider Aadhaar, the voter identity card and the ration card. It gave no direction to accept them. This is how the Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 describes the hearing.

title: Bihar's draft roll
what_changed: The draft roll was published, with claims and objections open to 1 September. No name was to be deleted from the draft without a hearing and a written order.

title: The names left off must be published
what_changed: The Court recorded the Commission's agreement that the roughly 65 lakh names left off the draft would be published with the reason for each, district by district and searchable by EPIC number, online and on panchayat and block notice boards, and that the public notice would say a claim could be made with a copy of Aadhaar.

title: Political parties brought in
what_changed: Twelve political parties were made parties to the case and told to have their booth agents help voters file forms with any of the 11 documents or Aadhaar. This is how the 2026 judgment describes the order.

title: Claims after the deadline
what_changed: The Commission told the Court that claims, objections and corrections could still be made after 1 September and would be considered up to the last date of nominations. The Court directed the chairman of the Bihar State Legal Services Authority to have the district legal services authorities send para-legal volunteers to help voters and parties file them online. This is how the 2026 judgment describes the order.

title: Aadhaar becomes the 12th document
what_changed: The Court directed that Aadhaar be accepted as the 12th document, as proof of identity and not of citizenship, with the authorities free to check that it is genuine.

title: The Commission follows the order
what_changed: The Commission told the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar that Aadhaar is the 12th document, for identity and not citizenship.
documents: ECI letter of 09.09.2025 to CEO Bihar

title: Bihar's final roll
what_changed: The final roll was published with about 7.42 crore electors. Appeals lay to the District Magistrate and then the Chief Electoral Officer.

title: Twelve more states and union territories
what_changed: The revision was extended to Andaman and Nicobar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Puducherry, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, on the June order with changes. No documents were to be collected while forms were filled. The form instead asked for the elector's, or a relative's, entry in the state's last intensive revision, and notices would go after the draft only to those who could not be linked to it. For every form not returned, the booth officer was to record a probable reason (absent, shifted, dead or duplicate). The Form 6 declaration was changed, and booth officers were to carry at least 30 blank copies of Form 6 with it.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: Which old roll counts
what_changed: Each state's form is linked to the roll of its last intensive revision, and the Commission fixed which year that was. West Bengal, Kerala, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Goa go back to 2002. Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Bihar go back to 2003. Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh go back to 2005, and Arunachal Pradesh to 2006. Tamil Nadu has two, 2002 for 197 seats and 2005 for 37.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: The first Phase II schedule
what_changed: Enumeration from 4 November to 4 December 2025, the draft on 9 December, claims to 8 January 2026, notices to 31 January, and the final roll on 7 February 2026.
documents: ECI order of 24.06.2025 and letter of 27.10.2025, as published by CEO Kerala

title: Assam gets a different revision
what_changed: Assam was given a "Special Revision" in place of an intensive one, with house-to-house checks from 22 November to 20 December 2025 with a register pre-filled for the booth officer, the draft on 27 December, claims to 22 January 2026, and the final roll on 10 February 2026. The pages read give no reason for the difference.
documents: ECI letter of 17.11.2025 to CEO Assam (instructions listing, eci.gov.in)

title: Anta gets its own dates
what_changed: Rajasthan's Anta seat could not follow the 27 October schedule because a bye-election was under way, so it was given its own, with enumeration from 8 December 2025, the draft on 12 January 2026, claims to 11 February and the final roll on 12 March 2026.
documents: ECI letter of 27.11.2025 for 193-Anta, CEO Rajasthan

title: Every Phase II date moves a week
what_changed: All twelve states and union territories got one more week, with enumeration to 11 December, the draft on 16 December, claims to 15 January 2026, notices to 7 February, and the final roll on 14 February 2026.
documents: ECI order of 30.11.2025, as published by CEO Goa

title: Lists before the draft
what_changed: Chief Electoral Officers were told to give party booth agents the booth-wise lists of those absent, shifted, dead or duplicated before the draft, and to put them online, searchable by EPIC number, after it.

title: Seven move again
what_changed: At the request of their Chief Electoral Officers the dates moved again, with drafts on 19 December for Tamil Nadu and Gujarat, on 23 December for Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Andaman and Nicobar, and on 31 December for Uttar Pradesh. Kerala had already been moved to a draft on 23 December. The same release also lists Gujarat among the states keeping the 16 December draft, and does not name Puducherry.

title: The "logical discrepancy" list
what_changed: The Court said names in the "logical discrepancy" category may be displayed at panchayat, block and ward offices, that documents could be filed through an authorised representative such as a booth agent, that the Commission allow ten more days from display, and that the Madhyamik admit card may be accepted.

title: More officers to help
what_changed: 8,505 state officers were to report to the district and registration officers to assist them, with the final decision left to the registration officers, and at least a week beyond 14 February was given for scrutiny.

title: Judges decide the claims
what_changed: Using its powers under Article 142, and with the parties' consent, the Court gave the deciding of claims and objections about inclusion to judicial officers of West Bengal, helped by judicial officers from Jharkhand and Odisha, acting "for and on behalf of this Court". This is how the Court's orders of 2 and 13 April 2026 describe the order.

title: West Bengal's final roll, with 60 lakh held back
what_changed: The final roll was published with 60,06,675 names marked "under adjudication", to be added by a supplementary list if the judicial officers approved them.
documents: CEO West Bengal, press note CEO/PN-05/2026

title: Appeals go to tribunals
what_changed: Orders of the judicial officers could not be appealed to any executive officer. Appeals were to go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges, to be notified by the Commission in consultation with the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.

title: Nineteen tribunals
what_changed: Nineteen appellate tribunals were working. Appeals decided by 21 and 27 April were to be given effect through a supplementary roll before polling, and a pending appeal gave no right to vote.

title: The rest of the country
what_changed: The revision was ordered in 16 states and 3 union territories, covering the whole country except Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, whose dates would be announced later. Eight separate schedules were set. Notices after the draft would go to those not linked to the last intensive revision, or with a discrepancy in the linking, and lists of those noticed were to be published.
documents: ECI press note ECI/PN/086/2026 of 14.05.2026 (PIB) | Copy of the ECI order of 14.05.2026 (district site)

title: The Supreme Court upholds the revision
what_changed: The Court disposed of the petitions. It held the revision traceable to section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324, proportionate, and its document list, with Aadhaar added, not arbitrary. The Commission may enquire into citizenship only for electoral purposes and must refer doubtful cases to the competent authority of the Central Government. People domiciled in Bihar whose names were wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate may seek judicial review.

title: Mizoram avoids Sundays
what_changed: Mizoram's draft moved from Sunday 5 July to 4 July 2026, and its final roll from Sunday 6 September to 7 September, at its Chief Electoral Officer's request.
documents: CEO Mizoram press note of 04.07.2026 | CEO Mizoram press releases

title: Karnataka three weeks later
what_changed: Karnataka's draft came out on 24 August 2026, not 5 August, with enumeration running to 17 August, claims to 23 September and the final roll due on 27 October, not 7 October.

title: Maharashtra four weeks later
what_changed: Maharashtra's draft came out on 31 August 2026, not 5 August, with claims to 30 September and the final roll due on 4 November, not 7 October.

title: Documents at the door
what_changed: For people sent notices as unmapped or for logical discrepancies, booth officers would collect documents at home and upload them for the registration officer, and such people need not come to the office. A hearing would be held only in exceptional cases, as the registration officer decides, preferably online, and a family member authorised by the elector could attend. The Commission said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision had been upheld by the Supreme Court, and that outside the revision the forms of the 1960 Rules apply. Claims were extended in Delhi to 30 October and in Maharashtra to 12 October 2026.

title: Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya extended
what_changed: Andhra Pradesh's notices run to 10 October and its final roll is on 16 October 2026. Meghalaya's final roll moves to 26 October 2026.

title: A drive to find the names left off
what_changed: Publishing Uttarakhand's final roll, its Chief Electoral Officer set out the Commission's directions for what follows. Booth officers are to compare the roll from before the revision with the current one, list the electors who were on the first and are not on the second, visit them at home and help those still eligible to fill Form 6. The lists are to be shared with the booth agents of the recognised parties, and booth and special camps held, including for people in night shelters, labour colonies and the homeless.
documents: CEO Uttarakhand, press note PN 63/2026 of 03.10.2026
